name: Ethan Liu
tagline: ECE student at Carnegie Mellon University (integrated B.S. and M.S., expected May 2028), seeking hardware internships and co-ops in IC design, physical design, and design verification.

projects.title: 256x16b SRAM Design
projects.sub: Full-custom memory in Cadence Virtuoso, 45nm GPDK (18-622)
bullets: Designed a single-port 256-word by 16-bit SRAM in the 45nm GPDK process against four targets: under 24 FO4 access time, under 2.0 mW, a repeated cell area under 1600 λ², and cell area efficiency above 50%.
Laid out the SRAM cell as compactly as the DRC rules allow and built a 4x4 tiled array to extract the repeat distance, area, and X and Y dimensions and show tiling and contact sharing.
Completed DRC/LVS-clean layouts of the decoder, cell I/O, and control signal generator and integrated them with the cell array into a DRC/LVS-clean top-level layout.
Built schematics with wire parasitic models and ran read and write critical path and noise margin simulations.
Meets every constraint at the TTTT, TTLH, and TTHL corners, verified with an extensive testbench covering all test vectors.
projects.skills: Cadence Virtuoso, Spectre, schematic and layout, DRC/LVS, parasitic modeling, corner simulation

projects.title: RTL-to-GDS Flow and PPA Analysis
projects.sub: Signed MAC datapath with Cadence Genus and Innovus
bullets: Synthesized a pipelined signed 16x16 multiply-accumulate unit in Cadence Genus using TCL-driven flows that swept clock targets and cell types, weighting the critical path group to close worst negative slack.
Quantified a 1.6x faster critical path at roughly 5x the leakage, and a 200 MHz clock push that cost 8.6% more area and 12% more energy per cycle.

Ran the full Innovus flow (placement, clock tree synthesis, hold fixing, routing, signoff) to GDS, comparing post-signoff timing, area, and power against synthesis and checking for setup and hold violations.
Customized floorplanning and pin placement with TCL and scaled the flow to a 2x2 MAC array, assigning macro pins and clock entry to minimize block area.
projects.skills: Cadence Genus, Cadence Innovus, TCL, static timing analysis, PPA analysis

projects.title: Digital Datapath Design and Physical Layout
projects.sub: Custom IC design in Cadence Virtuoso, gpdk045
bullets: Designed a master-slave flip-flop and multi-stage datapath in the gpdk045 45nm process and drew the layout, reaching a DRC/LVS-clean 65.265 µm², within the 75 µm² constraint.
Ran parasitic extraction and static timing analysis in ADE Explorer, root-causing a setup violation against a 2.4 GHz target clock.
projects.skills: Cadence Virtuoso, ADE Explorer, DRC/LVS, parasitic extraction, timing analysis

projects.title: Assertion-Based Verification of Encrypted Calculator IP
bullets: Verified an encrypted RPN calculator IP (8-entry stack, 6 operations, 4 error outputs) without a reference model, using a 10-category fault model and 32 directed tests.

Wrote 36 concurrent assertions from 28 properties using implications, local variables, and reset-disabled checks, plus a protocol and stack-depth tracker that predicts errors without copying stack contents.
Detected injected faults in all 7 faulty design variants (dropped carry, one's-complement negation, no-op swap, non-sticky error flags) with zero false alarms on the fault-free model.
projects.skills: SystemVerilog, SVA, Synopsys VCS, DVE, fault modeling

projects.title: Network on Chip (NoC)
bullets: Designed a synchronous Network-on-Chip at the FSM-D level with Node and Router modules, a custom FIFO, and round-robin arbitration, supporting concurrent packet transfers across a 2-router, 6-node topology.
Verified the design in VCS across functional, stress/load, fairness, and performance test categories, passing every category.
projects.skills: SystemVerilog, FSM design, arbitration logic, functional verification, VCS

projects.title: RISC240 Multiplication Coprocessor
projects.sub: Microarchitecture and RTL design, 16-bit RISC-V-derived CPU
bullets: Implemented a multiplication coprocessor in SystemVerilog and integrated it into the datapath and control logic of a 16-bit RISC-V-derived CPU.
Wrote assembly test programs and validated them in an instruction-level simulator, then synthesized the design and debugged timing and control interactions on FPGA hardware.
projects.skills: SystemVerilog, computer architecture, assembly, hardware debugging

projects.title: Matrix Multiply Accelerator
bullets: Designed a pipelined 128x128 matrix-vector multiply-accumulate in SystemVerilog on a Spartan-7, meeting 100 MHz timing and finishing in under 512 clock cycles.
projects.skills: SystemVerilog, pipelining, Vivado, static timing analysis

projects.title: IC I/O Test Harness (TinyTapeout)
bullets: Contributed to board-level design for a chip test harness supporting TSMC 180nm/65nm tapeouts, building component libraries in Fusion 360 and KiCAD, selecting level-shifter ICs against datasheet specifications, and running ERC on the schematics.
Worked in a 4-person board team inside a 12-person project, documenting design trade-offs and contributing to BOM development and part sourcing.
projects.skills: Fusion 360, KiCAD, ERC, component selection, BOM development

projects.title: 125 kHz RFID Reader System
bullets: Designed the reader coil and tag-powering circuitry for a passive 125 kHz tag, then built the analog band-pass and low-pass demodulation chain to recover baseband data.
Wrote C firmware to decode 40-bit tag IDs, with the analog and digital stages operating in one signal chain.
Debugged the filter stages through iterative bench measurement with an oscilloscope, multimeter, and bench power supplies until the data was recovered reliably.
projects.skills: Analog circuit design, filter design, embedded C, oscilloscope, multimeter, soldering

projects.title: Self-Playing Guitar
bullets: Led CAD and embedded design for a self-playing guitar, building a modular electromechanical interface of SolidWorks-modeled solenoid housings, servo mounts, and a linear-actuator linkage.
Wrote Arduino firmware on an ESP32 to coordinate servo and linear-actuator motion and completed all electrical wiring, delivering a working prototype that played a clean chord.
projects.skills: SolidWorks, ESP32, Arduino, servo and actuator control, wiring, system integration

projects.title: Field Weakening Model
projects.sub: Carnegie Mellon Racing (Formula SAE), electric vehicle team
bullets: Modeled field weakening in MATLAB and Simulink for the team's high-voltage electric motor system, varying it to measure its effect on torque, power, and speed.
Found a vehicle speed gain of over 20% and showed that field weakening holds constant power at higher speeds at the cost of torque.
projects.skills: MATLAB, Simulink, motor control, modeling and simulation

projects.title: Cache Lab
projects.sub: Cache simulator and matrix transpose optimization in C (18-213)
bullets: Wrote a cache simulator in C and optimized a matrix transpose for cache performance.
Transpose results: 35,456 cycles (32x32) and 33,881,344 cycles (1024x1024).
